children: , the largest U.S. bank by assets, forecast mid-to-high-teens growth in investment-banking fees and markets revenue for the third quarter, Reuters reported. Shares were down approximately 0.9% at $349.50 Wednesday, based on the latest quoted price, rather than the earlier $353.64 level.

Co-President Doug Petno pointed to healthy corporate confidence and a strong deal pipeline as key drivers behind the outlook. Merger activity remains active, while JPMorgan's trading franchise is also positioned for another solid quarter. Petno also said CEO Jamie Dimon remains deeply involved in running the bank following the promotion of Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents.

The picture adds an important valuation check: JPMorgan's $349.495 share price sits 10.13% above its GF Value of $317.35, suggesting investors are already paying a premium for the bank's earnings momentum and franchise strength. Second-quarter investment-banking fees jumped 30% and markets revenue rose 35%, so even mid-to-high-teens growth this quarter would still be strong, just against a tougher comparison. JPMorgan's edge remains diversification: when lending gets harder, investment banking and trading can still carry more of the load.

title: JPMorgan Gains as Trading Growth Reaches High Teens
